name: @kku/shared
//exports: The root barrel re-exports subpaths that reach node:crypto / aws-sdk, so a `'use client'` React component cannot import runtime values from it. `./pipeline/program-phases`, `./scholar/parse` and `./scholar/disclosure` are published as explicitly client-safe subpaths (pure functions + types, no node:* and no SDK imports) — the first for the two admin pipeline pickers, the second so the profile page validates a pasted Scholar URL with the SAME parser the API rejects it with, the third so the deep-dive drawer, the print view, the Gotenberg PDF and the AUN-QA evidence pack all state the Google Scholar caveat in the same words, rather than second copies that drift. Only bundler-style resolvers (apps/web, esbuild) read this map — apps/api, apps/ingestion and packages/db use moduleResolution 'node' and still resolve via `main`.
//exports-resolve: `./src/scholar/resolve` is spelled with `src/` ON PURPOSE, and it is the one key in this map whose spelling is a workaround rather than a preference. Its consumers are packages/db, apps/api and apps/ingestion, which typecheck under moduleResolution 'node' — that resolution ignores this map and finds the file only through a deep path, so `@kku/shared/scholar/resolve` does not typecheck there (same finding as search-parse, recorded above). The deep path typechecks, but at RUNTIME Node honours this map and refused it with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED (measured 2026-09-09 from packages/db, both require and dynamic import). Listing the deep specifier as its own key is what makes one spelling work in both places. The module itself is client-safe — its only `search-parse` import is type-only, so no bundle pulls cheerio through it — but it is deliberately NOT in the barrel: the boundary stays a rule rather than a per-import judgement about which imports happen to be erasable.
//exports-search-parse: `./scholar/search-parse` is the OPPOSITE case: it is published as a subpath precisely so it is NOT in the barrel. It depends on cheerio, a large server-only HTML parser, and nothing client-reachable may pull it. Keep it out of src/scholar/index.ts. TWO KEYS POINT AT IT, and that is deliberate. Measured from packages/db on 2026-09-09, all four ways round: `@kku/shared/scholar/search-parse` RESOLVES at runtime but does NOT typecheck (moduleResolution 'node' ignores this map), while `@kku/shared/src/scholar/search-parse` typechecks but was refused at runtime with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Neither spelling worked in both worlds, so the runner (packages/db/src/scholar-fetch.ts, Task 5) could not import it at all until the deep `src/` spelling was listed as its own key — the same workaround already recorded above for ./src/scholar/resolve, and the same measured failure pair. This adds NO client exposure: `./scholar/search-parse` was already in this map, so a bundler could already reach cheerio through it; the second key is another spelling of an already-open door. The guarantee that keeps cheerio away from client components was never this map — it is the module staying out of src/scholar/index.ts and therefore out of the barrel. `packages/shared/test/scholar-search-parse.test.ts` asserts both: that the key exists, and that nothing under apps/ imports this module.
//exports-jobthai: `./jobthai/parse-sheet` follows the same rule as `./scholar/search-parse`: published as a subpath precisely so it is NOT in any barrel. It depends on `xlsx`, a large server-only spreadsheet parser, and nothing client-reachable may pull it. Keep it out of src/jobthai/index.ts. Both the short and the deep `src/` spelling are listed for the same measured reason recorded above: apps/api and apps/ingestion typecheck under moduleResolution 'node', which ignores this map and needs the deep path, while Node at runtime honours the map and refuses a deep path that is not a key. `./jobthai` itself is pure (no xlsx) but is also kept off the root barrel, so the boundary stays a rule rather than a per-import judgement.
